get.description:
Identify the board with board_id to keep the request at one upstream
lookup, or with the username plus slug pair. A slug call resolves the
board id first; that resolution is cached for an hour on the slug pair
and is never billed separately, so one request is always one charge and
a repeat call to the same board costs the single feed lookup. Only pins
are returned: advertisements and other non-pin modules are filtered out.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: 1-based page number, 1 to 30000. `start` is (page - 1) x rows, so the deepest offset this reaches is (30000 - 1) x rows — beyond the entire measured inventory (556,435 listings, 244,746 agencies) at the default rows of 20. That inventory is not reachable at every rows value: past the ceiling with rows still on the table, matches remain behind the client, and the response then says so under next.page_ceiling_reached. A page beyond the ceiling is refused with a 422 rather than sent upstream.

parameters.name: rows
parameters.description: Listings per page, 1 to 50. Default 20.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: One of destaque, masnuevos, menorprecio, or mayorprecio. Default destaque. menorprecio returns ascending prices and mayorprecio descending. Any other value is rejected rather than sent upstream.

parameters.name: price_min
parameters.description: Lower price bound. Requires price_max as well: a one-sided band is rejected rather than returning an empty page. The bound carries no currency, so it is read in the site default currency — the currency block of the response says so explicitly. Amounts are never converted.

parameters.name: price_max
parameters.description: Upper price bound. Read in the site default currency, which this API does not publish. Amounts are never converted.

parameters.name: seller_type
parameters.description: Restrict by seller, for example dueno-directo or inmobiliaria.

parameters.name: price_availability
parameters.description: con-precio for listings that show a price, sin-precio for those that do not. Any other value is rejected.

parameters.name: region
parameters.description: Published search region code, for example zona-norte. Listed in the filter catalog returned with every search.

parameters.name: partido
parameters.description: Published partido code, for example partido-de-pilar or capital-federal. Every code the server publishes is accepted and every other is rejected rather than returning an empty page. Given a region as well, the partido must belong to it; a cross-region pair is rejected for the same reason.

parameters.description: published (default) or sale-agreed. Sale-agreed rows carry asking price only; Daft.ie publishes no transacted price.

parameters.name: sort

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: 1-based page number. Page N starts at row (N-1) x per_page, so consecutive pages never overlap and never skip rows. The paging block is restated in these terms: currentPage, pageSize, totalPages, displayingFrom/displayingTo and nextFrom all describe per_page pages, not the 50-row pages Daft.ie itself sends.

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: Rows to return, 1 to 50. Default 50. Daft.ie always answers with a full 50-row page; rows beyond this count are dropped so the returned row count matches the request. Note the cost: one upstream call always buys 50 rows, so walking a full result set with per_page=10 spends five times the calls that per_page=50 does for the same rows.

parameters.name: price_min
parameters.description: Lower price bound. Applied to salePrice on sale sections and rentalPrice on rent sections.

parameters.name: language
parameters.description:
Same invariant `refRules()` enforces on every other address
position: no path segment may be a bare `.` or `..`. Without it
`?language=..` reached the wire as a literal `..`, because
`rawurlencode()` percent-encodes `/ ? # :` but leaves `.` alone
(RFC 3986 unreserved) and Guzzle's path filter only escapes
invalid characters — it never removes dot segments. The host is
a class constant so this was never a host escape, but it was the
one address position in the platform missing the guard.

parameters.description: Trending window: daily, weekly or monthly. Defaults to daily.

parameters.name: spoken_language_code
parameters.description: Filter by the language developers speak, e.g. en. Omit for no filter.

parameters.description: 2-letter country code for localization (e.g., us, gb, de, fr)

parameters.name: hl
parameters.description: 2-letter language code for results (e.g., en, es, fr, de)

parameters.name: amenities[]

parameters.name: eco_certified
parameters.description: Filter for eco-certified/sustainable hotels only

parameters.name: special_offers
parameters.description: Filter for hotels with special offers/deals

parameters.name: property_types[]
parameters.description: Filter by property type IDs (SerpAPI list, comma-separated). Example: 12 (Beach hotels), 1 (Apartments)

parameters.name: brands[]
parameters.description: Filter by brand IDs (use brands[].id from response)

parameters.name: bedrooms
parameters.description: Minimum number of bedrooms (1-20, vacation rentals only)

parameters.name: bathrooms
parameters.description: Minimum number of bathrooms (1-20, vacation rentals only)

parameters.name: next_page_token

parameters.name: property_token
parameters.description: Property token for a specific hotel (from search results)

For incremental syncing, compare the updatedAt field rather than createdAt.

matched_upstream.description:
The upstream count covers sale and rent together, because the deal type split happens
after the rows come back. It is published under its own name rather than as `total` on
a scoped query, where a caller sizing a crawl from it would count rows this endpoint
then drops.

enum: For rent, a price ceiling of 10,000 NIS is applied as a server-side narrowing because Madlan has no server-side deal type filter. Rent and sale prices barely overlap.
Full-text search runs against the listing description in Hebrew, so query text is passed through as raw UTF-8.
For sale and for rent are separated after the fact: Madlan rejects every server-side deal type field, so rows are matched on their own deal type after they return.

matched_upstream is Madlan's own count and covers sale and rent together, because the deal type split happens here and not upstream. On a deal_type query total is null for that reason: there is no honest total for the scoped subset, and publishing the mixed one would size a caller's crawl from rows this response drops.

Madlan serves search results from a rotating shard set, so consecutive pages can overlap or skip. This endpoint returns one page and reports its coverage; use the listing corpus endpoint to enumerate ids.

prefixItems.const: Only the id and name are listed here, because Madlan declares the price range as a required field that resolves empty for projects without a published price, which fails the whole page when selected. Fetch a project to read its price range and details.

This enumeration surface is stable across repeated calls, so paging it is safe. Madlan also exposes a browse surface for projects that returns a different set on every identical call and ignores filters without reporting it. That surface is published separately at /api/madlan/projects/browse for parity with Madlan's own site, and is never paged or filtered here because its results cannot be reproduced.
No filters are accepted. Narrow the returned rows yourself, or fetch individual projects.

parameters.name: ids
parameters.description: Up to 50 comma-joined listing ids to hydrate in one lookup, for example 20622-M6020965. At least one id is required: an empty ids value is rejected with a 422 rather than answered as an unfiltered search. Default route only: the rich route answers it with an empty page, so rich=true with ids is rejected with a 422. An id batch is a single fixed window upstream, so no other parameter applies to it: every filter, page and per_page sent alongside ids is rejected with a 422 rather than dropped.

enum: The source answers at most the first 10000 rows of a cell. Subdivide it and run one billed request per sub-area. The fanout axes are business_type, property_type, city and neighborhood, but neighborhood only filters an area you already hold a slug for - it is not a partition. The partition method is a lat/long radius grid at 3 km or tighter: inside a radius every returned listing is geo-referenced, so the grid cannot silently drop rows it can see. It is not an exhaustive sweep - listings with no coordinates are unreachable by radius (roughly 2 percent of sale inventory and 6 percent of rent inventory carries none), and no partition of this source is provably exhaustive.

partition_method.const: To split a large city, subdivide by radius instead: pass latitude, longitude and distance to /search. Inside a radius every returned listing is geo-referenced (measured 100% at 2, 3, 5 and 8 km), so a radius grid cannot silently drop rows it can see, which makes it far better than this vocabulary. Start the grid at 3 km or tighter: at 5 km a large cell already exceeds the row ceiling again. It is still not an exhaustive sweep: listings carrying no coordinates are unreachable by radius (roughly 2 percent of sale inventory and 6 percent of rent inventory carries none), so no partition here is provably complete. get.description: Fetch any URL and extract structured data including title, meta description, keywords, favicon, social links, all links on the page, emails, phone numbers, images, body text, and detected languages. Meta keywords are always a JSON array of strings: content="php,,laravel" returns data.keywords=["php","laravel"]. Empty entries are omitted, remaining order and duplicates are preserved, and missing or all-empty metadata returns []. Set javascript=true for client-rendered pages. In JSON responses, url is the requested URL (with a protocol added if omitted), and final_url is the destination after redirects. Relative links, image URLs, and favicons are resolved against final_url, preserving non-default ports. Query-only references keep the page path: ?page=2 at https://example.com/catalog/page?old=1 resolves to https://example.com/catalog/page?page=2. Relative dot segments are normalized: /catalog/../item becomes /item and /catalog/./item becomes /catalog/item. Reference queries and fragments are preserved. Default HTTP(S) ports may be omitted from resolved relative URLs. Only HTTP(S) destinations are returned; absolute HTTP(S) references are left unchanged. If the destination URL is unavailable, the URL used for the fetch is returned. Returns the site's HTTP status code separately so you can distinguish site errors (404, 500) from infrastructure errors. Use response_type=markdown to get only the page content as clean markdown.

parameters.description: Set to true to include the raw HTML in the response. Default: false. Ignored when response_type=markdown

parameters.name: javascript
parameters.description: Set to true to execute page JavaScript before extracting content. Rendering uses Obscura first and can fall back to Cloudflare Browser Rendering if navigation fails. Default: false

parameters.name: response_type
parameters.description: Set to "markdown" to return only the page content as clean markdown text. When set to markdown, only the markdown content is returned (not JSON). Default: json

cursor the loop cannot advance, so the honest answer is false.
